old_caption:
The video opens with a serene view of a bridge spanning over a partially frozen river. The sky above is a clear blue, dotted with fluffy white clouds, creating a picturesque backdrop. On the right side of the frame, a green road sign reads "PLATTE RIVER," indicating the location. The river below is mostly covered in ice, with patches of open water visible. Bare trees line the riverbank, suggesting it might be late autumn or early spring.

As the camera moves forward, more of the bridge comes into view. The bridge has a concrete structure with metal railings on both sides, providing a sturdy path for vehicles. Two cars can be seen driving on the bridge, one approaching from the distance and another further ahead. The road appears to be well-maintained, with clear lane markings. The surrounding landscape includes more bare trees and some distant buildings, adding depth to the scene.

caption: A forward-looking view from the right edge of a bridge spans the Platte River. A green PLATTE RIVER sign on two rusty posts stands among leafless trees and brush in the right foreground. A concrete barrier and metal guardrail divide the road from the calm, cloud-reflected water. To the left a multi-lane highway runs toward a flat horizon under a blue sky of scattered cumulus clouds, and the camera translates steadily forward along the bridge. This forward motion produces clear parallax. The sign, its posts, and the bare branches slide continuously rightward across the frame. The distant white structure and the road's vanishing region drift only slightly. A dark SUV, entering from the left edge early on, travels ahead in the left lane and gradually shrinks as it recedes toward the horizon, while two tiny vehicles near the horizon remain there, shifting right with the rest of the scene. Apart from the perspective shift, the river and clouds stay unchanged. The forward travel continues.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
